prerequisites: Basic skills and competencies in power electronics, power plants, electric machines, and control systems, and automation, either accomplished at his/her incoming student profile and CV or by passing the related subjects of the first semester.

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Knowledge of the principal mathematic tools used in the analysis, modelling and simulation of power systems.
Use of computers and digital processors in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control and supervision of power systems.
Critical analysis of the information coming from the sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Asses the risks of the use of electrical energy, as well as those of industrial installations, understanding the necessity of safety elements, protections and signalling in power systems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Characterization and modelling of the main energy sources and electric power loads
Ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modelling of electrical power systems.
Characterization, operation and design of electronic topologies and control methods for electric energy conversion
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems
Acquire the basic knowledge of power electronics to analyse and design electrical power systems
Ability to analyse and understand the design of electric drives
Understanding the fundamental characteristics, as well as advantages and drawbacks of electrical and hybrid traction systems compared to combustion engines
Acquire the knowledge of power electronics needed to analyse and design electrical and hybrid traction systems

Learning how to deal with the specific instrumentation material of a power systems laboratory. Given the characteristics of this laboratory, safety issues when handling such equipment will be emphasized.
To integrate previous knowledge to develop a project of some importance.
Develop learning skills and independent work.
Presentation of a report/project in public.

syllabus_topics: Oral presentation of the final report
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: Final grade = 0.50 * PR + 0.30 * OP + 0.10 * ST + 0.10 * PA. A minimum attendance of 50% is required. If the minimum attendance requirement is not fulfilled or any mandatory element (PR, OP, ST) is not completed, the final grade will be the minimum between 4.0 and the result of the formula. Extraordinary assessment consists of submitting required projects (PR), an oral presentation (OP), participation along the course (PA) and/or additional tasks or simulations (ST), with weights proportional to the ordinary assessment.
bibliography: Different materials will be provided depending on the assigned project.
